<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Before we jump into Salesforce, let’s take a moment to define some common provider types. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Some providers work individually, while others are part of a group practice. Individual doctors or groups can have a singular specialty, or you may find a group with a range of specialties under one roof. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The physical location where the provider sees and treats patients is a facility. Some providers may work at multiple facilities, as part of one or more groups. The facility where they provide service may be different from their billing (or remittance) address. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Finally, providers and groups can be either participating or non-participating. Their network status indicates whether they are contracted to provide services for the plan. Whether a service is covered or requires additional documentation often depends on whether the provider is participating or non-participating.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Knowing these differences will help you identify provider types in Salesforce and navigate provider account records.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> </Block> </Content> </Document>
